historical_record.description: The Works Progress Administration began the preliminary planning of the arboretum in Golden Gate Park.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved Prentiss French's 1949 master plan for the Strybing Arboretum and Botanical Gardens, amended to make room for an Exposition and Exhibit Hall in its southeast corner, by the Ninth Avenue and Lincoln Way entrance, and for a Pan-American Grove in its western part.
The Noble Collection of dwarf conifers and its memorial plot were to be dedicated at the Strybing Arboretum on the afternoon of December 3, the Recreation and Park Commission was told.

The Recreation and Park Commission accepted the Strybing Arboretum Society's gift of an information kiosk for the arboretum, worth about $3,000, and approved its drawing by Gardner A. Dailey and Associates.
The Garden of Fragrance in the Strybing Arboretum was dedicated, its flowers and herbs labeled in Braille for blind visitors.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved in principle the plan, presented by the arboretum's director, for the Jennie Zellerbach Memorial Garden, to be given to the department for the Strybing Arboretum.
The Recreation and Park Commission approved the plan by Richard Splenda of Splenda and Yamamoto, landscape architects, for a Garden Work Center in the arboretum's Demonstration Gardens.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved the final plans by Yuill-Thornton, Warner & Levikow for the Helen Crocker Russell Library, an addition to the arboretum's existing building paid for by private subscription through the Strybing Arboretum Society, which was to build it and deed it to the city.
The Recreation and Park Commission approved a $10,000 agreement with Eckbo, Dean, Austin & Williams, landscape architects, for the John Muir Trail in the Strybing Arboretum.
The Recreation and Park Commission awarded the $14,989 contract for the second phase of site work in the arboretum's Demonstration Gardens to Cagwin and Dorward.
The Alice Eastwood Garden in the Strybing Arboretum, given by the San Francisco Garden Club, was dedicated on May 7, as a commissioner reported to the Recreation and Park Commission.

The Biblical Walk in the Strybing Arboretum, a gift marking the 125th anniversary of Temple Emanu-El, was dedicated on May 18, as the arboretum's director reported to the Recreation and Park Commission.
